previous_paragraph: where  α is a degradation factor ranging from 1 for a healthy structure to 0 for a completely damaged structure, and ζ is the damping ratio. Note that the degradation factor relates specifically to the loss in stiffness. This simplified stiffness-degradation model is needed to obtain a theoretical formulation of the stability boundary. In practice, degradation may also change other properties, particularly damping. However, increased damping has been shown to improve RTHS stability [31]. Therefore, neglecting any additional damping introduced by degradation represents a conservative assumption with respect to this effect.
actual_paragraph: To address the nonlinear and time-varying nature of structural degradation, a short-window linear approximation is used to keep the analysis tractable and suitable for online evaluation. Although this method may not be accurate during brief intervals where properties change rapidly, it is typically accurate before and after such events, and during periods where degradation evolves slowly.
next_paragraph: With the real-time hybrid simulation (RTHS) framework blocks defined, a vRTHS is performed to evaluate various stability indicators. This analysis considers a three-story reference building where a portion of the first story acts as the physical substructure represented by an SDOF frame. More details on this study are provided in section 6. The stability analysis begins by simulating a healthy structure (α=1) and then progressively reducing the degradation factor, α​, to simulate the accumulation of damage. The level of specimen degradation is increased in this way to allow the system to approach an instability and illustrate the target behavior.
